body:
## Problem

Multipart image uploads larger than 20 MB are silently truncated before they reach an OAuth (ChatGPT) account. Measured on a deployment built from v0.2.18, `POST /v1/images/edits` with `stream=true`, `quality=low`, `size=1024x1024`, served by an OpenAI OAuth account:

| Upload | Result |
|---|---|
| Valid PNG, 23,530,018 bytes | HTTP 400 `invalid_image_file`, `"Invalid image data."`, `param: images[0].image_url` |
| Valid JPEG, 47,486,671 bytes | HTTP 200 and an edited image, but upstream only received the first 20 MB of the JPEG, so the source it edited was cut off partway down |

The JPEG case returns a wrong result with no error, and the user is billed for it.

## Root cause

- `parseOpenAIImagesMultipartRequest` reads every part through `io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(part, openAIImageMaxUploadPartSize))` with the limit at 20 MB, and never checks whether the part was longer.
- The OAuth Responses path (`buildOpenAIImagesResponsesRequest`) and the direct Codex path base64-encode `parsed.Uploads`, so the truncated bytes are what upstream receives.
- `parseGrokMediaMultipartRequest` uses the same limit and the Grok edit payload is built from its uploads the same way.
- The API key path forwards the raw multipart body through `rewriteOpenAIImagesMultipartModel` (`io.Copy`, no limit), so the same request succeeds or fails depending on which account type serves it.

## Fix

- `openAIImageMaxUploadPartSize` is 50 MB, the per-image limit OpenAI documents for GPT image model edits ("each image should be a `png`, `webp`, or `jpg` file less than 50MB").
- The OpenAI images parser reads one byte past the limit and returns `multipart field "image" exceeds the 50 MB per-part limit`; the handler already maps parse errors to 400 `invalid_request_error`.
- The Grok media parser reads parts whole. Its body is already bounded by the gateway request body limit (`gateway.max_body_size`, 256 MB by default), and `/v1/images/*` requests for Grok models pass through the OpenAI parser's check first.
- The images routing log line now records each upload's content type and size (`upload_parts=[image/png:23530018]`), so an upstream image rejection can be matched to the file that caused it.

## Tests

New file `internal/service/openai_images_upload_limit_test.go`:

- `TestParseOpenAIImagesRequest_MultipartKeepsUploadAbove20MB`: a 21 MB part comes back byte-for-byte. Before the fix it came back as 20,971,520 bytes.
- `TestParseOpenAIImagesRequest_MultipartRejectsUploadAbovePartLimit`: a 50 MB + 1 byte part is rejected with the message above.
- `TestParseGrokMediaRequest_MultipartKeepsUploadAbove20MB`: the same 21 MB part is kept whole by the Grok parser.

`go test ./internal/service/ ./internal/handler/...` passes.

End to end on the patched build, the same 23.5 MB PNG through the same OAuth account returns 200 with a single `image_edit.completed` event, and a 50 MB + 1 byte upload gets the 400 from the gateway without reaching upstream.

title: fix(images): reject oversized multipart uploads instead of truncating them
